finding: Canonical MLR-Agent establishes S4=A through a mandatory outside-and-then research path: recent external literature and challenge synthesis feed a prospective proposal/methodology which is then implemented by the experiment stage and returned into later research operation. MLR-Bench publishes rich first-party stepwise proposal scores and end-to-end paper-quality results, but those surfaces do not isolate that S4 relation. Proposal evaluation stops before downstream operational benefit, while end-to-end evaluation mixes S4 with coding-agent experimentation, execution reliability and paper writing. No matched public treatment disables or varies the native literature-to-proposal adaptation path while preserving the downstream execution membrane, so no direct canonical S4 observation is admitted.
reassess_if: MLR-Agent publishes a matched treatment that disables, replaces or materially varies the native external-literature/proposal adaptation relation while holding the downstream experiment membrane materially fixed
public evidence measures whether a prospective MLR-Agent adaptation changes later experimental capability or research outcome under a recoverable matched protocol
a matched public benchmark compares MLR-Agent native S4 with another canonical native or adapter-preserved S4 system under one common adaptation/return protocol
